asDecan.p: Each sign is cut into three slices of ten degrees, the decans, and each slice gets a planet and a small card of its own. Your Sun sits in the first ten degrees of Leo, the sign at its freshest. In the Golden Dawn order that slice goes to Saturn, which is an odd planet to find there. Leo is fixed fire, ruled by the Sun, warm and proud and happy to be looked at. Saturn is the planet of limits and earning things the slow way. It rules Aquarius, straight across the zodiac, so in Leo it's in detriment, which just means it's working against the grain of the place and you can see the effort. The next slice along is Jupiter's, the Six of Wands, with the laurel wreath and the parade. After that comes Mars and the Seven, a man on a ridge fending everyone off. Yours comes before the parade. Strength is your Sun card for Leo as a whole, and the Five of Wands says which kind of Leo you are.

You rarely get to coast on charm, and you stopped expecting to a long time ago. Before a job interview you've over-prepared, with notes on the company's last three annual reports, because you assume you'll have to win the room before it warms to you. At a family dinner, when your brother tells the story of the holiday and gets the laugh, you're the one quietly correcting the dates. You notice who got thanked in the all-staff email, and if it wasn't you, it sits with you for the rest of the afternoon. There's plenty of Leo pride in all this, and you do want to be seen. Saturn just makes the pride do its homework first, so being noticed for something you didn't work at barely counts. At a friend's wedding you're half listening to the speech and half rewriting your own.

What people tend to miss is that you're a very good sparring partner. Put you in a room of strong opinions, a writers' room, a school committee, a netball team with three people who all want to be captain, and you'll argue hard and then shake hands at the end without carrying a grudge home. Look at the picture on your card. Five lads swinging long sticks at each other and nobody's bleeding. That's the kind of fight you're good at. You also make the people around you better. A colleague who sits next to you for a year usually leaves sharper, partly because you pushed back on their draft and partly because they saw how much went into yours. And you can take a hard note. If an editor tells you the second half doesn't work, you'll sulk for an evening and have it rewritten by Wednesday.

The less obvious trouble is what happens once the recognition actually turns up. You've spent so long expecting to fight for it that when it's simply handed over, a promotion, a round of applause, a friend saying your lasagne is the best they've had, you don't quite trust it. You find the flaw, or decide they're only being kind, and the goalposts move again. You can also make a contest out of moments that don't have one. Your partner mentions a good week at work and you find yourself listing yours. A friend rings to say they're engaged, and before you've finished congratulating them you've already checked where you are against them. You're not proud of that and you'd never say it out loud, but it's there, and the people closest to you can sometimes feel it in the room.

When things go wrong you dig in and work harder. You get passed over, or a relationship ends, or a project you'd put a year into gets shelved, and your first move is to prove somebody made a mistake. Longer hours, a new course, a gym membership, a very well-formatted spreadsheet. A week on, the heat has usually gone out of it and you're tired and flat, and you've stopped mentioning it to anyone, because Leo hates being seen to struggle and Saturn tells you it's your own job to fix. So the people around you get a version of you that's polite and shut, which can be harder on them than a row would be. What helps is letting one person see the wobble before you've sorted it. After that, something with nothing to win in it, a swim, cooking for friends, a film you've seen ten times.

You're slow to let it show. Early on you tend to come across as warm but careful, and that's Saturn checking whether the other person is serious before the full Leo generosity comes out. Once it's out it's a lot. Birthdays planned weeks ahead, the loyalty, backing them up at a party whether they were right or not. What partners don't expect is how much you like being argued with. Someone who agrees with everything you say can bore you within a month, and a good-natured row in the car about which way to go feels, to you, a lot like closeness. A partner who grew up in a house where raised voices meant real trouble won't hear it like that, so it's worth asking early what arguing meant in their family. You also need to hear you're appreciated more often than you'd ever ask. So ask. "I'd like to hear you're proud of me" is a perfectly reasonable thing to say.

You're built for work where there's a standard to meet and someone to measure yourself against. Competitive fields suit a lot of people with this decan, law, sales, sport, the performing arts, anywhere with an audition or a pitch or a table of results at the end of the quarter. You're at your sharpest when someone across the office is doing well, and a quiet team with nobody to compare yourself to can leave you oddly flat. Bosses usually notice you're thorough before they notice you're talented, which annoys you. You're also often the one who stays back to fix the slides the night before the big presentation, and then minds a great deal when someone else gets up and gives it. Raise that before the meeting. Say plainly that you want your name on the work, because Saturn in Leo will otherwise wait years to be noticed.

At twenty this decan is often all effort and very little ease. You're auditioning for everything, a bit prickly about rejection, and inclined to think anyone who got there faster must have had help. It's a hard age for Saturn in Leo, because the recognition hasn't had time to arrive yet. By the mid-thirties the picture usually shifts. The years of work start to show, as a reputation or a skill people pay for, and most people with this slice of Leo begin competing with their own last effort and stop watching the person at the next desk so closely. The fifties are often kind here, since Saturn tends to do its best work late. A lot of early Leos I've seen end up as the coach or mentor in their field, the one who tells a young talent the work isn't ready yet and then gives up a Saturday to help fix it.

Once a week, on the same evening, write down one thing you did well that nobody saw or thanked you for. The report you checked twice, the call you made to your aunt, the argument you decided not to start. Just a line, in one notebook kept for it. On the first of each month, read one entry out loud to someone you trust and let them say something nice about it. Don't correct them or play it down. Say thanks and change the subject.
